questions: In fully visible middle frames, are exactly three pens visible on the white carrier?
Does each pen show a visible black cap-like part at its lower end?
Does any pen show an exposed pointed writing tip where the black cap-like part should be?
Are the three pens parallel and similarly oriented on the carrier?
Are the black cap-like parts on the same end of all three pens?
Is any pen reversed or upside down compared with the other pens?
Is any pen tilted or diagonal compared with the other pens?
Does the carrier move smoothly from LEFT to RIGHT while the pens remain stable relative to it?

question_answers.evidence: In frames 00:05 to 00:08, exactly three pens are clearly visible on the white carrier.
The leftmost pen does not show a black cap-like part at its lower end; instead, it shows a pointed tip.
The leftmost pen shows an exposed pointed writing tip at the bottom, whereas the other two have black caps.
All three pens are arranged vertically and are parallel to each other.
The middle and right pens have the black cap-like part at the bottom, but the left pen has a pointed tip at the bottom.
The pens are not reversed relative to each other in a way that suggests a simple orientation error; the left pen is missing its cap.
All pens are vertical and aligned; none are tilted or diagonal.
The carrier moves smoothly from the left side of the frame to the right side, and the pens remain stationary on it.

parsed.reason: The leftmost pen clearly lacks the black cap-like part present on the other two pens and instead shows an exposed pointed tip, fitting the MISSING_CAP anomaly definition.
